lead.headline: U.S. and Iran trade fire over the Strait of Hormuz
lead.dek: CENTCOM hit launchers it says were set to mine the strait; Jordan intercepted eight missiles fired back at bases hosting U.S. forces.
body: American forces struck two Revolutionary Guard rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island on Sunday, and Iran answered before dawn Monday with ballistic missiles aimed at U.S. forces at the King Hussein and Al-Azraq air bases in Jordan - the first direct exchange of fire between the two countries in a month.

U.S. Central Command called the strike a 'limited, precise action' to keep Guard forces from laying sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, where American ships had been clearing shipping lanes; Iran's Fars news agency reported soldiers killed and wounded on the island without giving figures. The Guard named its reply 'Punishment of the Aggressor' and said it also downed a U.S. MQ-9 drone over the strait.

Jordan's military said it intercepted eight missiles that crossed into its airspace at dawn, and no injuries were reported at either base. President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was 'not looking for war' but would 'never sit still in the face of any aggression.' The strait ordinarily carries about a fifth of the world's oil.

art.caption: The Falcon Heavy carrying the Roman Space Telescope crosses the risen sun Sunday morning, its exhaust column trailing to the clouds.

briefs.headline: Experts doubt Venezuela oil deal will move gas prices
briefs.summary: The joint venture gives the U.S. 55% of output from about 65 billion barrels of largely undeveloped reserves at cost; analysts say production is years off and any price effect is 'far on the horizon,' as Congress spars over the deal.

briefs.headline: House returns with four weeks to head off a shutdown
briefs.summary: Members are back Monday to take up a continuing resolution ahead of the Sept. 30 funding deadline; Republicans also plan a reconciliation package carrying money for the Iran war. Massachusetts holds its midterm primary Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Federal plan cuts Arizona's Colorado River share 27%
briefs.summary: The mandatory reductions run through 2028 after the basin states failed to agree, with cuts up to 40% possible later; Phoenix-area utilities say customers will pay for recycling plants and pipelines that replace the supply.

briefs.headline: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario for U.S. users
briefs.summary: The lake now shows as 'Lake America' to American users after the Trump administration's name change entered the federal names database; Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered with a billboard reading 'Lake Ontario - Now and Always.'

briefs.headline: Nepal-Tibet flood toll passes 900 with thousands missing
briefs.summary: Nepal has recovered 903 bodies and lists 4,247 missing five days after the Rasuwa flood, with 16 dead and 546 missing in Tibet; 85 Americans were unaccounted for as of Sunday, and Washington activated $3.6M in emergency aid.

briefs.headline: Russia threatens Ukraine's grid as depot strike toll hits 38
briefs.summary: Moscow said it has begun preparing 'massive strikes' on energy infrastructure; Saturday's drone strike on a munitions depot at Myla, near Kyiv, killed 38, and Ukrainian drones set the Kirishi refinery burning in Leningrad region.

briefs.headline: Norway sets King Harald's funeral for Sept. 9
briefs.summary: The service is at Oslo Cathedral at 1 p.m. led by the church's presiding bishop; Haakon VIII swears his oath in parliament Tuesday, the same day the public begins filing past the casket at the palace chapel.

briefs.headline: Civilian negotiator freed Kenscoff hostages; police face probe
briefs.summary: Community leader Luckson Jean walked into gang territory to bring out the 13 women and children released with UNICEF support; Haiti's police chief ordered an investigation into negligence or complicity, and more than 50 remain held.

briefs.headline: Settlement fund nears $50M invested as state marks overdose day
briefs.summary: The West Virginia First Foundation, distributing about $1 billion in opioid settlements, says it will have put nearly $50M into prevention, treatment and recovery by year's end; overdose deaths are down 41.6% from pre-pandemic levels.

briefs.headline: Child care shortage tops the Chamber's Greenbrier summit
briefs.summary: More than 100 providers have closed in recent years and care runs about $800 a month per child, panelists said at the 90th Business Summit, in a state where workforce participation sits below 54%.

briefs.headline: Recovery groups open September on Magic Island
briefs.summary: West Virginia Sober Living held its fifth annual Kickoff to Recovery in Charleston on Sunday, adding an inaugural 5K ahead of National Recovery Month, with speakers and program tables in the heat.

regional.item: The Mason Youth League opened fall ball this weekend under new field lights - 57 teams and nearly 700 players.
Nitro Elementary may close its vandalized playground Monday if burned equipment and broken glass cannot be made safe.

away.item: Twenty-seven veterans and Guard family members urged Gov. Scott to back a Defend the Guard bill after 200 Vermont airmen deployed overseas.

hotspots.item: Surf City put its annual backflow-testing program out for proposals Sunday - about 300 devices town-wide, with bids due Sept. 30 at town hall.

briefs.headline: CNC pairs business students with entrepreneur mentors
briefs.summary: The College of New Caledonia's new mentorship program launches this fall alongside its revised business administration program, with Northern Innovation Network director Mary Mytting as the first mentor.

briefs.headline: Highway 1 reopens through the Fraser Canyon after seven weeks
briefs.summary: A two-kilometre stretch near the Alexandra Tunnel has run single-lane behind pilot cars since Wednesday, with delays up to 30 minutes; the Brunswick Complex fires that closed the route in July are still out of control.

briefs.headline: Three by-elections today test Carney's minority math
briefs.summary: Voters fill vacant seats in North Vancouver-Capilano, Beaches-East York and Chicoutimi-Le Fjord; the Liberals hold 170 seats, two short of a majority, and the B.C. race between Braeden Caley and Stephen Curran looks closest.

briefs.headline: Roman Space Telescope launches on dark-energy hunt
briefs.summary: The NASA flagship lifted off Sunday at 7:26 a.m. ET on a Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center and separated from the rocket to fly on its own, opening a three-month cruise to an orbit a million miles out.

briefs.headline: CAR T-cell therapy quiets severe rheumatoid arthritis
briefs.summary: All six patients in a Charite Berlin trial improved after the cancer-derived treatment and three reached medication-free remission, Nature Medicine reported; autoantibodies fell sharply with only mild, manageable side effects.

briefs.headline: Study finds most recurrent UTI diagnoses are wrong
briefs.summary: Only 15% of 253 women diagnosed with recurring urinary tract infections had bladder or tract problems; most showed hormone-driven inflammation treatable without antibiotics, researchers reported in The Journal of Sexual Medicine.

briefs.headline: Anthropic's automated researchers patch model misbehavior
briefs.summary: An AI system that searches the literature, proposes training methods and tests them improved a target model on all 10 misalignment benchmarks tried, the company reported, closing 85% of a deception gap against 20% for human researchers.

briefs.headline: Deepfakes of late-night hosts spread while shows are dark
briefs.summary: Fabricated clips of Jimmy Kimmel and Jon Stewart are drawing hundreds of thousands of views; one Stewart fake sat on TikTok more than two months without an AI label, and researchers say a single photo and 15 seconds of audio suffice.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore has the morning's sky at 7:15.
kicker: September's sumo rankings landed in Tokyo this morning; the sport page carries them.
